# Sammādiṭṭhika Sutta (Iti 71 (It 3.22 PTS It 59))

**ID:** Iti 71 (It 3.22 PTS It 59)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Sammādiṭṭhika Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammādiṭṭhika Sutta* ("Having Right View", Iti 71) is a short prose-and-verse discourse located in the third division (Tikanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.22, PTS It 59) [Windisch 1889]. In this discourse, the Buddha explains that he speaks not from hearsay but from what he has personally known, seen, and realized: namely, having seen beings endowed with bodily, verbal, and mental right conduct, who do not slander the noble ones, hold right views, and perform deeds born of right view (*ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), being reborn after the breakup of the body in a good destination, a heavenly realm (*sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā*) [Windisch 1889]. The prose statement concludes with the standard transmission formula (*etam-atthaṁ bhagavā avoca, tatthetam iti vuccati*) followed by verse teachings on setting the mind and speech rightly [Windisch 1889].

 The stock description of rebirth according to karma and right view (§2.1–2.2) is shared extensively with major discourses in the *Dīgha Nikāya* (e.g., DN 2, DN 10, DN 25, DN 28), the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 12, MN 73, MN 130), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 6, AN 8, AN 10), as well as Abhidhamma and exegetical works such as the *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4), *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 16), *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), and *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 14) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects a machine match between segment §3.1 and the Tibetan *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (D0119) [DharmaNexus].
